findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Replace `.venv/bin/pytest` in all AC and Testing verification commands with a platform-agnostic form (e.g. `python -m pytest`, `uv run pytest`, or a `rtk`-native invocation that abstracts the venv path) so the commands work on Windows as well as POSIX.
evidence: Plan quotes: `rtk .venv/bin/pytest -q tests/unit/test_code_review_project_criteria.py -k eval --collect-only` (Testing section) and five AC bullets all repeat `rtk .venv/bin/pytest -q ...`.
`.venv/bin/` is the POSIX venv layout; Windows uses `.venv\Scripts\pytest.exe`.
The supported matrix includes the Windows platform cell.
findings.finding: Every Acceptance Criterion and Testing section verification command hard-codes `.venv/bin/pytest`, a POSIX virtual-environment path. On Windows the pytest binary lives at `.venv\Scripts\pytest.exe`; the POSIX path does not exist, causing the verification command to fail with a file-not-found error before any test runs.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria (all five AC bullets) and Testing section: `rtk .venv/bin/pytest -q tests/unit/test_code_review_project_criteria.py -k eval`
scenarios: Windows platform cell: a developer or CI runner on Windows executes any AC verification command; the shell cannot find `.venv/bin/pytest`, returns a file-not-found error, and all five ACs are unverifiable as written.
findings.suggested_fix: Change `rtk .venv/bin/pytest` to `rtk python -m pytest` (or whatever `rtk`'s cross-platform test-invocation convention is) in every AC bullet and the Testing section.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a one-sentence positive rationale in the Approach section explaining why the code-review arm is added inline to `calibrate_criterion` (e.g., to reuse the shared recall/kappa/stability metric math without duplication) rather than as a separate function.
evidence: Plan says: 'In eval.py, use the existing calibrate_criterion(..., repo_root=None, ...) parameter. Select the code-review arm only when repo_root is not None and criterion_id in code_review.registry.effective_criteria(repo_root).' — describes WHAT but not WHY this boundary was chosen over alternatives.
No sentence in the plan explains why extending the single calibrate_criterion function (rather than, e.g., a separate calibrate_code_review_criterion) is preferable.
findings.finding: The plan does not state a positive rationale for why the chosen approach — an inline membership-check arm inside the single calibrate_criterion function — is the right interface boundary, as opposed to structurally different alternatives. Its absence means an implementer cannot confirm the design intent, and a reviewer in a later pass cannot evaluate whether the trade-offs were considered.
scenarios: An implementer choosing between arm-in-existing-function vs. separate function defaults to whatever is easiest, potentially adding an unnecessary duplicate of the metric math.
A future reviewer or diff author cannot confirm this was a deliberate design choice vs. an oversight.
findings.suggested_fix: Add to the Approach paragraph on `eval.py`: 'This arm is added inline to `calibrate_criterion` rather than as a separate function because the metric math (recall/false_accept/kappa/stability) is identical for both gates and duplication would create a maintenance burden.'
